title: Make notes navigable with Markdown
goal: Organize notes while preserving quotations, deadlines and unknowns.
explanation: Formatting can help people find information, but a polished hierarchy can make invented conclusions look authoritative. Keep original text beside the formatted version and check that headings do not imply decisions that were never made. Markdown is plain text; different renderers support different features.
sampleInput: Raw notes: “Repair table idea. Nia said ‘Keep the first event small.’ Venue inquiry due Friday. Tools list not assigned. Budget proposal $80, not approved. Need insurance check. Next discussion Tuesday.”
prompt: Organize these notes in Markdown using one H1 title, H2 sections for Confirmed actions, Proposals and Open questions, a blockquote for the exact quotation, bold deadlines and a horizontal rule before next steps. Preserve the unassigned owner and unapproved budget. Do not invent decisions.
workedExample: Expected structure: # Repair table planning; ## Confirmed actions → venue inquiry due **Friday**; ## Proposals → $80 budget, not approved; ## Open questions → tools owner and insurance check. The quotation must retain its wording and attribution.

steps.title: Mark the source states
steps.text: Identify quote, commitment, proposal and unresolved question before formatting.

steps.title: Generate plain Markdown
steps.text: Keep the raw syntax so you can inspect #, >, ** and --- directly.

steps.title: Preview safely
steps.text: Use the activity’s text-only rendered preview; raw HTML is not required.

steps.title: Audit the meaning
steps.text: Compare all named dates, ownership and budget status with the raw notes.

steps.title: Test portability
steps.text: Open the Markdown as plain text and check that the structure is still understandable.

checks: The quote is exact and the proposed budget remains unapproved.
Heading levels are consistent and deadlines are emphasized without changing them.
Unassigned actions remain unassigned; no formatting implies a false decision.
commonMistakes: Making a proposal look like an approved action by moving it under the wrong heading.
Assuming every Markdown renderer handles tables or raw HTML identically.
offline: Write the Markdown by hand and compare the raw syntax with a paper outline.
reflection: Which heading choice could most easily change how the notes are interpreted?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. The quote is exact and the proposed budget remains unapproved.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Heading levels are consistent and deadlines are emphasized without changing them.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Making a proposal look like an approved action by moving it under the wrong heading.
